result:
I now have the full picture. Here's the lifecycle.

## 1. Admin submits the invite

The admin fills `InviteMemberForm` (`src/components/domain/member/invite-member-form.tsx`), which client-side gates the form on `can(actor, "member:invite", ...)` (`src/lib/permissions.ts`) purely for UX, and validates the input against `inviteMemberSchema` (`src/schemas/member.ts`, built on `emailSchema` + `invitableRoleSchema`) before calling the server action.

The server action `inviteMemberAction` in `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts` (wrapped by `withAction`) re-validates with the same `inviteMemberSchema`, then does the real authorization: `can(actor, "member:invite", { kind: "member", orgId, memberId: PENDING_MEMBER_ID, targetUserId: actor.userId, targetRole: input.role })`. If that fails it throws `ForbiddenActionError`. It then calls `consumeRateLimit(input.orgId, "member:invite")` (`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`), and finally re-derives seat usage via `getOrganizationSummary` + `getPlanLimits` (`src/config/plan-limits.ts`) to reject if the new invite would exceed the plan's seat quota (`PlanLimitError`). Only after all three checks pass does it call `inviteMember` from `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts`.

## 2. Invitation is minted

`inviteMember` delegates to `inviteMembers`, which repeats the authorization and quota checks server-side against the DB truth (not trusting the action layer alone): `assertOrgScope`/`assertCan` (`src/lib/tenant.ts`, `src/lib/permissions.ts`), `consumeRateLimit` again, then loads the org via `orgRepo.findOrgById`, computes `seatsUsed = countActiveMembers + countPendingInvitations` (`member-repository.ts` / `invitation-repository.ts`), and checks `wouldExceedLimit` against `getPlanLimits(org.plan)` — pending invitations count against seats, per the file's header comment.

For each invite it generates `randomToken(32)` (`src/lib/hash.ts`, `crypto.randomBytes` base64url) and stores it via `invitationRepo.insertInvitation`, but only `hashToken(token)` (SHA-256) is persisted to the `invitations` table (`src/server/db/schema/members.ts`), alongside `orgId`, `email`, `role`, `invitedBy`, `expiresAt` (now + 14 days, `DEFAULT_EXPIRY_DAYS`), and null `acceptedAt`/`revokedAt`. The **raw** token — the only thing that can reproduce that hash — is what would go into the emailed link (`/invite/[token]`); the DB never sees it in plaintext. An `emit("member.invited", {...})` event fires on the in-process event bus (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`), which `activity-service.ts`'s subscriber (`subscribe("member.invited", ...)`) turns into an activity-log row ("Invited x as role"). Note: nothing in this codebase actually subscribes to `member.invited` to send mail — `src/emails/invite-email.tsx` and the `renderTemplate` machinery in `src/emails/render.ts` exist but `renderTemplate` is never called; delivery in this build is a log-only stub anyway (`sendEmail` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` just logs `email.sent`).

## 3. What travels in the link vs. what's stored

Stored in `invitations`: token **hash**, email, role, org, inviter, timestamps, expiry. What travels in the mail link: the **raw** token as a URL param, `/invite/[token]?org=<slug>`. Possessing the raw token is the sole credential — there is no signed session tied to it.

## 4. Colleague opens the link

`src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx` first validates the token's shape only (`invitationTokenSchema.safeParse` — length/charset), never resolving it against the DB at this point (explicitly noted in the file's header comment — only `InvitationService` may look up a token, and only when consumed). It then calls `getSessionPrincipal()` (`src/lib/session.ts`); if unauthenticated, it redirects to `/login?next=/invite/<token>`. Once signed in, it renders `InviteAcceptForm` (`invite-accept-form.tsx`), a client component whose only job is to POST the raw token back via `acceptInvitationAction`.

## 5. Accepting the invitation

`src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts` validates with `acceptInvitationTokenSchema`, requires a session principal, then calls `acceptInvitation(userId, { token })` in `invitation-service.ts`. This runs **unauthenticated with respect to org scoping** — there's no `Actor` yet, so every check is against the stored row itself: it looks up `invitationRepo.findInvitationByTokenHash(hashToken(token))` (the only repository read not scoped by `orgId`, since the token hash *is* the tenant credential), then checks in order `revokedAt === null`, `acceptedAt === null`, and `expiresAt > now`, throwing a specific error for each failure. If the user is already a member it returns the existing membership idempotently. Otherwise it calls `memberRepo.insertMember(orgId, userId, invitation.role, invitation.invitedBy)`, marks the invitation accepted via `invitationRepo.markInvitationAccepted`, and emits `member.joined`.

Back in the action, `assertSeatAvailable` re-resolves an `Actor` via `resolveActor` (`member-service.ts`) now that membership exists, and re-checks `getOrganizationSummary`/`getPlanLimits` seat usage — since the org could have filled up between invite and accept — throwing `PlanLimitError` if seats are now over the limit (membership row still exists though; this is a post-hoc check, not a rollback).

## 6. What the rest of the system learns

`member.joined` is picked up by two subscribers: `usage-service.ts` (`subscribe("member.joined", ...)`) increments `seatsUsed` in the usage counters table, and `notification-service.ts` (`subscribe("member.joined", ...)`) notifies the org owner ("A new member joined"). `activity-service.ts` also has (elsewhere) a `member.joined` handler writing the activity feed entry. The client's `InviteAcceptForm` watches the action result and, on success, routes the browser to `/${orgSlug}` or `/orgs`.
